header: Which utility a line means, whatever the words. detect.ts answers exact asks ("gold rate today"): every word must be one the topic knows. This file answers the rest, for the reader who writes a whole sentence, in capitals, with a typo, with "please" and "sir", or in Hinglish: I score the line against what each topic SAYS it is (its `intent`: name, one sentence, words and near-words, plus its own key words) and name the utility the line is clearly about, or none. It runs in the browser, instantly, and sends nothing anywhere. This file names no topic: it walks the topics of src/tools/registry.ts. The score. Each informative word of the line (not a filler like "please", "tell", "the", not a bare number, not a place such as "Kolkata", which says where and not what) is matched against the words of a topic: exactly, as the same stem ("prices"/"price"), with one slip of spelling ("pettrol"), or by a long common beginning ("calculation"/"calculate"). A match counts the RARITY of the word (a word that only one topic uses is worth more than "price", which four use); an informative word the topic does not know counts against it. I call a topic CLEAR when its score is high, nearly every informative word is explained by it, and no other topic comes close: "PLEASE TELL ME THE CURRENT GOLD PRICE IN KOLKATA SIR" is clear (gold); "circular on gold loan" is not (a document search with one word of a topic), and I leave it to the search, or to the AI that is asked what the user means (src/lib/tools/intentAi.ts).

members.name: vocab
doc: Every word the topic uses of itself, lower case.

members.name: open
doc: How it is opened: its own page (a form), or the card that this typed line makes.

symbols.name: weight
doc: How much a matched word is worth: a word of one topic, 3.3; of four, 1.9; of ten, 1.2.

symbols.name: stem
doc: I take a plural or an ending off, so that "prices" and "price", "charging" and "charge" meet.

symbols.name: distance
symbols.sig: export function distance(a: string, b: string, max = 2): number
doc: The edit distance, with an early stop since the words are short.

symbols.name: similarity
symbols.sig: export function similarity(q: string, v: string): number
doc: How well a word of the line matches a word of a topic: 1 exact; .92 the same stem; .8 one slip of spelling (.7 two, in a long word); .65 a long common beginning; else 0.

symbols.name: informative
doc: Returns the words of a line that say WHAT is wanted (not fillers, not bare numbers, not places).

members.name: strength
doc: The rarity-weighted size of what matched.

members.name: confidence
doc: strength / (strength + a charge for each informative word of the line that the topic does not know): 1 when the topic explains every word.

members.name: unknown
doc: The informative words the topic did not know.

symbols.name: rankIntents
doc: Scores every topic against the line, best first.

symbols.name: clearIntent
symbols.sig: export function clearIntent(line: string): Ranked | null
doc: The utility a line is CLEARLY about, by my rule: a strong match (not a lone common word), nearly every informative word explained, and no other topic close; else null.

symbols.name: looksLikeSentence
doc: A few words of a sentence: these are the lines worth asking the AI about when the topics do not settle them.

symbols.name: maskForAi
symbols.sig: export function maskForAi(line: string): string | null
doc: The line as it may leave for the AI: long digit runs (a ticket, a phone, a PAN-like number) and e-mail addresses are blanked; null when the line is not for the AI at all (an ID query, too short, too long).

symbols.name: worthAsking
doc: Whether the AI is worth asking about this line: a few words, nothing that could only be a person's name or an ID (those go to the directory), and a line that may leave at all.

symbols.name: catalogForAi
doc: The list of utilities as the AI is shown it: one line each, "id | title: about".

behaviours: no line of the corpus opens the WRONG utility, by an exact reader or a clear intent
at least 90% of the ${total} arbitrary lines open the right utility with no AI at all (the rest go to the AI step)
the corpus covers every utility that has an intent
none of the 40 ordinary searches (names, ids, departments, circular titles, one-word lines) is taken for a utility by the clear-intent step
a plural, an ending, a slip of spelling and a long beginning all meet the word: prices/price, charging/charge, pettrol/petrol, calculation/calculate; unrelated words do not
fillers, politeness, places and numbers carry no weight: only what is WANTED is read
a rare word counts for more than a common one: 'gold' alone is stronger than 'price' alone
a line with a word the topic does not know is less sure of it: 'gold price' is surer of gold than 'gold price revision circular'
two topics equally near make no clear intent ('gold loan' is the gold card and the loan form alike)
a line of one word, or one word and fillers, is left to the exact readers and the search
the AI is asked only about a sentence that cannot be a name or an ID: a person's name (even of three words), a person by number, a question that is a document search is not excluded but a name is
a sentence is three words or more
long digit runs, phone numbers and e-mail addresses are blanked before a line leaves; short numbers stay
an ID query, a line that is too short or too long is never sent
the prompt carries the list of utilities (every id), the blanked line, the 'none' rule, and nothing of the user but the line
an ID query is not sent at all: the AI is not even called
the AI's reply is checked: a real id with a confidence is a pick; none, an unknown id, a missing or non-numeric confidence, prose and broken JSON are not
an AI that fails or hangs gives no answer, not an error
the route needs a signed-in user, can be switched off (TOOL_INTENT_AI=off) or has no key, limits a person to 12 a minute, remembers a line for an hour, blanks the line first, and logs nothing of it
the browser sends only the one line, never throws, and acts on a pick from a confidence of 0.6
